exposure: Enrollment in the West Virginia University Medicine Drug Free Moms and Babies Assist Connect and Encourage program (DFMB/ACE)
outcome: Breastfeeding at the time of discharge
cohort: Women with substance use disorder in pregnancy who delivered at a tertiary care center. The intervention group enrolled in the DFMB/ACE program from 2018 to 2019, while the control group (n=734) had a positive urine drug screen on admission but were not enrolled in the program.
finding: The DFMB/ACE program for women with substance use in pregnancy improved some perinatal outcomes, including a lower risk of preterm birth and higher birth weight, but did not significantly affect other outcomes like NICU admission, NAS, mode of delivery, or breastfeeding rates.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery rates were not statistically different between the intervention and control groups.
birth_weight: Intervention group: 2865.7 g, Control group: 2657.9 g
